Consider the quadratic form 
$Q(x)={x}_{1}^{2}-3{x}_{1}{x}_{3}-{x}_{2}{x}_{3}+{x}_{3}^{2}.$ 
Evaluate $Q(x)$ when $x=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 0 \\ -4\end{aligned}].$
feedback.worked_solution:
We are given that 

$$
x=[\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{2} \\ {x}_{3}\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 0 \\ -4\end{aligned}].
$$

Substituting this into the expression for $Q(x)$, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}Q(x) & ={x}_{1}^{2}-3{x}_{1}{x}_{3}-{x}_{2}{x}_{3}+{x}_{3}^{2} \\  & ={1}^{2}-3\cdot 1\cdot (-4)-0\cdot (-4)+(-4)^{2} \\  & =1+12+0+16 \\  & =29.\end{aligned}
$$
